chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever bequeaths one-third of his estate and is then killed by mistake, then one-third of his blood-money (diyah) is included in his bequest.'
ai.seo_question: Does blood money count towards the one-third bequest in Islamic inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies that the one-third bequest (hadiya) extends to the blood-money (diyah) received for unintentional homicide, treating it as part of the testator's disposable estate. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence for distinguishing between the fixed shares of heirs and the discretionary portion, ensuring the deceased's final wishes are honored even with compensation for death. It reflects the principle that diyah, like wealth, can be allocated according to the will up to the one-third limit.
